relevance_note: Single case report of a Blau syndrome patient with a NOD2 variant: "identified a previously unreported heterozygous mutation consisting of a G>A transition in exon 4 of the NOD2 gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; one in-scope person (the single unnamed patient, label 'patient'); JSON built with a short script, spans checked verbatim by script. Not extracted as a person: the N670K carrier(s) of ref 4, mentioned only as a variant associated with EOS with no individual-level fact. Variant printed only as protein shorthand 'E667K' and 'G>A transition in exon 4'; no cDNA, transcript or genomic description printed, so those fields are null/not reported. Variant type 'missense' recorded from the authors' description 'glutamic acid to lysine substitution' (the word 'missense' is not used). Pathogenicity recorded as the authors' 'Novel Mutation'/'previously unreported'; conservation and the proposed effect on auto-inhibition are in-silico/speculative, not a functional assay, so functional evidence is not reported. Inheritance not reported: 'sporadic' and 'no family history of similar disease' but no parental testing. Age at diagnosis taken as the age at presentation (12 years), since the abstract states she presented at 12 and was diagnosed on those findings; age at last evaluation not given (final follow-up 8 months after presentation). Discrepancy within the paper: the abstract says 'bilateral granulomatous anterior uveitis' while the case description says the right eye showed 'non-granulomatous anterior uveitis'; both recorded as observed rows (uveitis itself is not in dispute). Normal chest imaging recorded as 'abnormal chest imaging' excluded per D-27 (does not exclude interstitial lung disease). 'No vascular abnormalities' refers to the eye in context of vitreous haemorrhage; recorded as written and not used for the vasculitis checklist item. Elevated serum ACE is not ESR/CRP, so the inflammatory-marker checklist item is not reported.
